title: SCIM incremental delta sync, soft-delete quarantine, and audit enrichment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Large customer directories produce frequent partial failures during SCIM delta syncs (network blips, user-level conflicts, rate-limits). Current behavior either (a) retries aggressively and duplicates operations, or (b) marks whole sync as failed and misses deprovisioning, causing stale accounts.

Proposed solution: Implement an incremental delta-sync flow with three complementary features: (1) idempotent patch sequencing and per-object op_id to avoid duplicate applies; (2) a soft-delete quarantine for accounts/groups that appear removed from the identity provider but fail final deprovision steps — quarantined objects are visible in the admin console for manual review and automatic TTL-based purge; (3) enriched audit events emitted for every SCIM operation with delta_token, external_provider_id, op_id, conflict_reason, and retry_count to improve observability and postmortem analysis.

Scope: server-side SCIM connector logic, audit pipeline enrichment, Console UI hooks for quarantine review, and migration for existing tombstones. Does not include full UI polishing — initial admin UX will be a compact review table with bulk-approve/restore/purge actions.

Why different from existing work: focuses on reconciliation semantics for partial failures and admin-first quarantine flow (rather than only retries/backoff). Emphasizes audit enrichment to make root-cause analysis deterministic for large enterprise syncs.
acceptance_criteria: Delta sync applies SCIM patches idempotently: re-sent op_id is a no-op after first success
Soft-deleted users/groups moved to quarantine when final deprovision step fails; quarantine exposes created_at, ttl_until_purge, last_error
Audit events for SCIM ops include delta_token, op_id, external_provider_id, conflict_reason, retry_count
Admin console shows quarantine table and supports bulk-approve (finalize deprovision), restore, and purge
Automated TTL purge removes quarantined objects after configurable window (default 14 days) and emits final audit event
Integration tests cover simulated connector flaps, partial apply of group membership changes, and idempotency guarantees
No regression in existing SCIM throughput targets for small orgs (<10k users). Large-org runs measured and documented with perf numbers
implementation_notes: Add op_id UUID to every outbound SCIM patch; persist per-target-object last_applied_op_id with index to avoid duplicate application
Store quarantine records in dedicated table with indexed ttl_until_purge; avoid coupling to reconciliation tombstones used by other flows
Emit audit events to existing pipeline (structured JSON) with new fields: delta_token, external_provider_id, op_id, conflict_reason, retry_count
Connector backoff: implement connector-level token bucket to smooth bursts; hard-limit retry window for a single object to avoid infinite loops
Migration: backfill recent tombstones for last 30 days into quarantine with ttl based on original tombstone timestamp
Testing: unit tests for op_id idempotency; chaos tests simulating mid-sync DB restarts and network failures; e2e against Okta & Azure AD test tenants
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gate: scim_quarantine_v1 off by default
Internal dogfood tenants opt-in to feature-flag during Cycle 42
Phase 1: enable idempotent op_id handling and audit enrichment (no quarantine) for 10% of tenants
Phase 2: enable quarantine for low-risk tenants and expose console table; monitor metrics for 1 week
Phase 3: ramp to 100% after performance validation and security review
Rollback: on rising error-rate or quarantine explosion, disable quarantine flag and rely on idempotency + backoff
risks: Quarantine growth for noisy connectors could exhaust DB storage if TTL misconfigured
Incorrect op_id dedup logic could permanently drop legitimate operations if a bug exists
Audit pipeline schema change may break downstream consumers if not coordinated
Admin endpoints must be hardened with RBAC v2 controls; leaking quarantine access would be high risk
